sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376, 366 of IPC and under Sections 4, 9(g)(1)/10 of POCSO Act in connection with POCSO Case No.71 of 2020.
He has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Section 376 of IPC along with other sentences.

3. Heard, learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4. Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.
5.
It is alleged that the victim-girl was gang raped after she was kidnapped.
In evidence, it has come that the victim- girl died 2 to 3 days after she was recovered and handed over to the parents.
The statement of the victim-girl is on record.
We have gone through it, we are not dealing with it in details.
From perusal of the entire statement, prima faice, we feel that without her consent, in the manner in which the occurrence had occurred the same could not be possible.
Further, she in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she was taken to a temple where her marriage was solemnized also and thereafter she stay with this appellant.

sentences.text: 6. Considering the aforesaid fact, we are inclined to allow this interlocutory application.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellant, namely, Babli Singh @ Babla Singh @
Ritlal Singh is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Giridih in connection with POCSO Case No.71 of 2020 with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court, Giridih, once in every four months till the disposal of this appeal 7.
